newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end mixed on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end mixed on profit-taking.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mixed in active trading on Monday due to profit-taking following last Friday's sharp gains, traders said.
The key January 1997 contract ended at an intra-day low of 3,110 yuan ($374) per tonne, rising 10 yuan. It opened at an intra-day high of 3,193.
March rose 10 to 3,110, May fell 10 to 3,120, July was unchanged at 3,160, September dropped 60 to 3,250 and November rose 60 to 3,350.
Combined volume rose sharply to 72,100 tonnes from 15,100.
Traders said last Friday's sharp gains encouraged long position holders, but profit-taking pushed the contracts down late in the session.
"Large amounts of buying pushed the prices sharp up in the morning session, but profit-taking at high levels made soybeans lose most of the gains later in the day," one trader said.
"Trading volume rose sharply, which indicated more institutions had entered the soybean market," he added.
Analysts said it was hard to predict how soybeans will move in the short term due to dominance by speculative institutional trading.
